hook: Planning to upgrade? Build your next deposit inside an offset.
so_what: Own an investment? Ask whether an offset on that loan should hold your savings. Tax side with your accountant.

hook: Building with a mate? Don’t do it in your own names.
so_what: Ask your accountant about a trust or company before you sign anything together.

text:
Your current bank can often do what you need.

Need a top-up, or more for the build? Most people assume that means moving the whole loan.

Moving costs you: discharge fees, switching costs, a new application from scratch.

So we ask your lender first. We switch when the rate or structure is meaningfully better elsewhere. Not just to move it.

label: first home
hook: Don’t buy a brand-new apartment just to get the grant.

label: first home
title: The grant has a price
body: New apartments are often priced high for what they are. If you overpay by more than the grant is worth, it hasn’t helped you. Compare the two before the grant decides.

label: first home
title: Old, small block, no lift
body: Around 10 to 15 one- or two-bedroom units on a decent-sized block. No lift keeps body corporate costs down, and the land underneath can appeal to developers later.

label: first home
title: Read the fees first
body: Before a view sells you, ask why the body corporate fees are what they are. Low running costs and real land underneath tend to hold their value.

label: first home
headline: New with the grant, or older without it?
body: A 15-minute chat is enough to know where you stand.
